# Reading (locked before the Lean): lem41_M1_chain

Passage: proof of Lemma 4.1, manuscript/paper/sections/04-proof-wellposedness.tex lines 159-170: the displayed
chain for E sup |M^1|. The first link (E sup|M^1| <= c_BDG E[(int int e^{2s}|dY_{s-}|^2
|dU_s(e)|^2 N(ds,de))^{1/2}]) is BDG in quadratic-variation form; this unit covers the links after
it:
 (L2) E[(int_0^T int_E e^{2s} |dY_{s-}|^2 |dU_s(e)|^2 N(ds, de))^{1/2}]
        <= e^T (E sup_{t<=T} |dY_t|^2)^{1/2} (E int_0^T int_E |dU_s(e)|^2 N(ds, de))^{1/2}
      (pathwise: e^{2s} <= e^{2T}, |dY_{s-}| <= sup_t |dY_t|; then Cauchy-Schwarz in omega);
 (L3) E int_0^T int_E |dU_s(e)|^2 N(ds, de) = E int_0^T int_E |dU_s(e)|^2 nu(de) ds   by (2.1);
 (L4) = E int_0^T ||dU_s||^2_{L^2(nu)} ds.
(the c_BDG factor multiplies both sides of each link in the paper; stating the links without it
is equivalent since c_BDG > 0.)

Setting: section 2 standing setting; N the Poisson random measure with compensator dt nu(de)
relative to (F_t); integrals against N are pathwise integrals against the random counting measure
N(omega) on R_+ x E restricted to [0, T] x E (whether (0,T] or [0,T] is immaterial: N has a.s. no
atom at time 0). All quantities are nonnegative, values in [0, inf]; the chain holds as stated
in [0, inf] without finiteness, and with dY in S^2 and dU in H^2_N the right sides are finite.

Hypotheses: dY cadlag adapted (for (L2) only cadlag-ness / measurability is needed; the paper has
dY in S^2 in force); dU predictable, read through a P (x) E-measurable representative (needed for
(L3): (2.1) requires predictable psi >= 0); in force dU in H^2_N. A faithful Lean must state
(L3) for the P (x) E-measurable representative and the actual random measure N of the setting,
with (L4) the identification int_E |dU_s(e)|^2 nu(de) = ||dU_s||^2. A statement over a general
(not Poisson) random measure would be false for (L3); over a class including the paper's N it is
broader.

Constants: none besides e^T. Conclusion: the three links as (in)equalities in [0, inf].

## Standing setting
Standing setting (manuscript section 2, manuscript/paper/sections/02-model-assumptions.tex lines 1-11): a filtered
probability space (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0, dimensions
n, m, d >= 1, a d-dimensional (F_t)-Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N
on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, \mathcal E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Ñ = N - dt nu. (2.1): E int int psi dN = E int int psi nu(de) ds in [0, inf] for
predictable psi >= 0. Spaces (section 3): S^2 = cadlag adapted with E sup_{t<=T} |V_t|^2 < inf;
H^2_W = predictable R^{m x d} with E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 < inf; H^2_N = predictable L^2(nu;R^m)-valued
with E int_0^T ||U||^2 < inf, read through a P (x) E-measurable representative ((2.8), Fubini
isometry). c_BDG (section 4, lines 22-37): one universal constant, valid for cadlag local
martingales, at p = 1 (Davis form, quadratic-variation form) and p = 2; it is fixed before all
data (C's depend on it). "Supremum criterion": a cadlag local martingale with integrable running
supremum has zero-mean increments.

comparison.text:
# Comparison: lem41_M1_chain (Dissertation/PaperSpec/A/Sec4LocalMartingales.lean)

Setting and hypotheses: exactly those of Lemma 4.1 (same block as lem41_MW/lem41_M1), the
paper's section-2 setting with enlJoint. No constant (the c_BDG factor common to both sides of each
link is dropped, equivalent since c_BDG > 0).

Conclusion, three conjuncts in [0, inf]:
 (L2) E[(int_{(0,T] x E} ofReal(e^{2s} sum_k (dY^k_{s-})^2 sum_k dU^k_s(e)^2) dN(omega))^{1/2}]
      <= ofReal(e^T) (E sup_{t in [0,T]} |dY_t|^2)^{1/2} (E int_{(0,T] x E} |dU_s(e)|^2 dN)^{1/2}:
      the printed second link (line 164-165), with the pathwise integral against the counting
      measure N(omega) over (0, T] x E (N has a.s. no atom at time 0, and dU vanishes off [0, T]).
 (L3) E int_{(0,T] x E} |dU|^2 dN = E int_{(0,T]} int_E |dU|^2 nu(de) ds: the compensation formula
      (2.1) for the predictable nonnegative integrand |dU|^2 (dU marked predictable is in force).
 (L4) = sum_k markedEnergy dU^k = E int_0^T ||dU_s||^2 ds (markedEnergy integrates over [0, T]
      instead of (0, T], a Lebesgue-null difference).
These are exactly the links of the printed chain after the first, as (in)equalities in [0, inf].
The first link (BDG in quadratic-variation form) is excluded by the clause and the scope note.

Witness: lem_bpbsde_nonzero_hypotheses; the integrands e^{2s} |dY_{s-}|^2 |dU|^2 and |dU|^2 are
nonzero there (dU = 1_{(0,1]}, nu = delta_0, dY nonzero).

Coverage paragraph:
Coverage (claim A:lem4.1:M2-infinite-activity, acceptance/claims.json; passage
manuscript/paper/sections/04-proof-wellposedness.tex lines 139-187). The seven clauses state:
M^2's integrand has no square moments from H^2_N (nu != 0); with nu(E) = inf the jump-time
localisation does not exhaust [0, T]; M^2's integrand is predictable and nonnegative; M^2's
integrability and zero mean (read pathwise, Poisson integral minus compensator); M^W (local Ito
integral, bound, finiteness, zero-mean increments); M^1 (local compensated integral, bound,
finiteness, zero-mean increments); the links of the M^1 chain after the first. Together they state
the mathematical assertions of the passage with two exceptions: (a) the assertion of lines
140-141 that M^2 is a local martingale is stated by no clause: M^2 is read pathwise and only the
zero mean of its increments is stated (for M^W and M^1 the local-martingale property is carried by
IsLocalBrownianIntegral / IsLocalCompensatedIntegral, as the scope note says; that the terms of
(4.5) are M^W, M^1, M^2 is delegated to (4.5)); (b) the first link of the M^1 chain and the first
step of the M^W bound (BDG at p = 1, Davis's form) are not stated as links, by a recorded scope
decision (cited work); the end-to-end bounds they lead to are stated, with the same right sides.
No clause states something the passage does not claim: the reading of c_BDG as "every value at
least some c0 > 0" is a convention for the unfixed universal constant, not an extra claim. The
hypotheses of the M^W, M^1 and chain clauses are exactly those of Lemma 4.1 in force at this
point (dY cadlag adapted, dZ in H^2_W, dU in H^2_N, dxi in L^2(F_T), phi in L^2(Omega x [0,T]),
equation (4.4)); dY in S^2 is not assumed but enters through the finiteness conclusion, as in the
printed membership step; no more, no fewer. The scope decision is still marked scope_reviewed:
false.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. The Poisson integrals are pathwise integrals against N(omega) over (0, T] x E (N has a.s. no
   atom at time 0), and the dt-integral of (L4) is over [0, T] through markedEnergy (null
   difference).
2. Quantities are lintegrals of ofReal(...) in [0, inf]; |dY_{s-}|^2 and |dU|^2 are coordinate sums
   of squares; dY_{s-} = 0 at s <= 0 (null time).
3. The common factor c_BDG of the printed links is omitted (equivalent, c_BDG > 0).
4. Hypotheses are the full hypotheses of Lemma 4.1 (exactly those in force), although (L2) holds
   without them and (L3) needs only the predictability of dU.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement with the author's reading of the three propositions (lem41_MW, lem41_M1,
lem41_M1_chain): setting, hypotheses (exactly Lemma 4.1's), integrands, local-integral
reading, bounds, finiteness, zero means and the chain links match my comparison, and the witness
lem_bpbsde_nonzero_hypotheses does give nonzero integrands for M^W and M^1. Two remarks the
review should add. (1) Coverage: the review says the decomposition of (4.5) belongs to (4.5) and
that M^2 is read pathwise, but it does not note that the assertion of lines 140-141 that M^2 is a
local martingale is stated by no clause of the claim (lem41_M2_zero_mean states only the
integrability and the zero mean of its increments); for M^W and M^1 the local-martingale
property is carried by the local-integral definitions. (2) The c_BDG reading ("every value at
least c0", c0 = 9 by Lenglart's argument) treats c_BDG as some sufficiently large universal
constant; it does not assert the bound at a smaller constant valid in Davis's inequality. That is
faithful because the paper never fixes c_BDG's value (and needs it valid at p = 2 as well), but
the review should say that this is the reading, rather than "for every value of the paper's
constant".
